claims.text: Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 is initially in a single-phase high-temperature BCC state.
The phase behavior of Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 is governed by diffusion-mediated chemical ordering.
Al is the principal element responsible for the proposed chemical ordering.
Chemical ordering induces a local order-disorder transformation from the high-temperature BCC phase to an ordered secondary phase.
The ordered secondary phase may be B2, L21, or another ordered structure.
Moderate cooling provides sufficient time for atomic diffusion and ordering.
Post-cooling exposure below the high-temperature BCC stability limit can activate Al mobility.
Al-mediated local ordering nucleates an ordered structure within the BCC matrix.
Interactions of Al with Co, Fe, or Ni may contribute to local chemical ordering.
During moderate cooling, Al atoms diffuse and segregate within the BCC matrix.
Al segregation establishes locally ordered regions that favor formation of an ordered secondary phase.
Subsequent thermal exposure coarsens the ordered domains.
Coarsening of ordered domains produces a measurable secondary-phase fraction alongside the BCC matrix.
Rapid cooling suppresses diffusional ordering and preserves a predominantly BCC state.
Moderately cooled and thermally exposed samples will contain more ordered secondary phase than rapidly quenched samples.
The proposed ordered phase will produce superlattice reflections detectable by XRD.
Atomic-scale ordering will be observable by TEM.
The proposed mechanism should not operate when transformation is athermal or diffusion is too slow for significant ordering.
At very low post-cooling temperatures, negligible diffusion should suppress the proposed ordering transformation.
